newsitem.title: DENMARK: U.S. helps Danish bonds recover from profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: U.S. helps Danish bonds recover from profit-taking.

text.p: Danish bond prices rose in early Wednesday trade, encouraged by U.S. June retail sales data and expectations that German bunds had bottomed out.
"Tuesday's American retail sales numbers were received by the U.S. market better than expected and there has been a positive rub-off (here)," a dealer said.
At 0730 GMT the outgoing benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was up 0.09 point from Tuesday, at 113.52 yielding 5.94 percent.
Its successor, the seven percent 2007 bond was 0.13 point up, at 106.29, yielding 6.15 percent.
The spread from the Danish 2007 to the 10-year German bund was 54 basis points, unchanged from Tuesday, and dealers expected it to remain around 53 to 54 for the rest of the day.

They also expected trading to centre on long paper, 10 years and upward, with the central bank likely to take advantage of the rising prices to offer longer-dated maturities after having stayed out of the market for the past two days.
The crown eased slightly, to 3.8118 to the mark from Tuesday's 3.8100. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969650
